advert.title: IT Project Manager / Senior Project Manager (English Speaking)
advert.text:
### About GRADION

GRADION is a strategic partner for businesses pursuing growth through digital innovation and deep tech. The company uses an AI-first approach across AI, data, cybersecurity, robotics, and enterprise platforms. It reports 23+ years of expertise, 300+ specialists across seven countries, and 100+ enterprise clients.

### About the Role

Lead international IT delivery projects across long-term Dedicated Team engagements and Fixed-Price projects. Turn ambiguous requirements into executable plans, identify risks early, and help clients make decisions that keep delivery on track. This is a client-facing role requiring clear communication, constructive pushback, and practical use of AI tools.

### Responsibilities

- Lead IT delivery projects end to end, from planning through delivery, across Dedicated Team and Fixed-Price engagements.
- Turn client requirements into actionable plans with clear scope, assumptions, and success criteria.
- Serve as the main contact between clients, engineering teams, and internal stakeholders.
- Raise risks early and drive decisions with options and a recommendation.
- Manage change requests and prevent scope creep to keep Fixed-Price projects within scope, budget, and margin.
- Maintain a healthy delivery rhythm for Dedicated Teams through capacity planning, prioritisation, and continuous client alignment.
- Use AI tools for requirements review, risk analysis, reporting, and stakeholder communication, checking outputs before use.
- Identify account-growth opportunities and contribute to business development.
- Travel to client sites when useful for the project or relationship.

### Requirements

- University degree in IT, Computer Science, or a related field.
- 5+ years of IT development project-management experience.
- Hands-on experience running both Dedicated Team and Fixed-Price projects.
- Excellent international English communication.
- Experience working with cross-cultural, English-speaking teams.
- Track record translating unclear client requirements into deliverable scope.
- Confidence raising risks and difficult topics early.
- Daily comfort with AI tools and sound judgement about output verification.
- Proactive, adaptable, growth-oriented mindset.
- Hands-on technical experience or solid software-development process knowledge is a plus.

### Working Conditions

- Full-time, Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 18:00.
- Hybrid work.
- Ho Chi Minh City office.

fit: Senior Project Manager with 7+ years of experience delivering banking, fintech, and SaaS solutions in regulated environments.
Proven ability to manage end-to-end IT project delivery, ensure regulatory compliance, and lead cross-functional teams across multiple regions, including Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Africa.
Expertise in core banking systems, digital banking transformation, security-driven product development, and stakeholder management within financial institutions.
Brings advanced AI methods into day-to-day project delivery, designing LLM-driven workflows and prompting techniques to accelerate analysis, documentation, and decision-making across IT projects.

Lead end-to-end banking IT projects covering core banking systems, mobile banking, and digital transformation programs, ensuring full compliance with banking regulations, PCI DSS, and internal IT governance frameworks.

Coordinate cross-functional, international teams (developers, QA, business analysts, cybersecurity, external vendors) across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Africa, managing scope, timelines, risks, and dependencies on mission-critical systems.
Act as primary interface between IT, business stakeholders, and external partners; run regular stakeholder reviews and solution demonstrations.
Apply Agile / Scrum delivery practices, running sprint planning, backlog refinement, retrospectives, and daily stand-ups to maintain steady delivery cadence across cross-functional banking IT teams.

Prepare and present formal project status reports and steering committee presentations for management, consolidating delivery progress, risks, and key decisions across ~4 concurrent banking IT projects.

Maintain a formal risk register across active projects, proactively tracking, escalating, and mitigating risks to protect delivery integrity and governance compliance on mission-critical banking systems.
Designed and delivered 10 AI workshops for the eBanking department (~30 participants), driving practical and compliant AI adoption across the team.
Implemented a trading platform (Lao Forex Exchange) integrated into the internal financial system.
Led end-to-end integration of card services into digital banking platforms, driving alignment between upstream APIs, business requirements, and customer-facing delivery.

Mapped existing manual project manager and analyst workflows, decomposed them into structured, executable LLM logic, then built and deployed an agentic assistant autonomously tracking project progress, monitoring email activity, and issuing proactive deadline and follow-up reminders.

Rolled out the assistant to a 6-person cross-functional pilot team (2 business analysts, 1 product owner, 2 developers, 1 QA) to validate the branch's first AI-driven work process ahead of wider deployment. In active daily use, delivered with an internal user guide.
Led the development and rollout of PIN-code authentication for the mobile banking application, strengthening customer security.
Coordinated the integration of third-party services (Telegram) into internal banking systems within strict security constraints.
Designed and launched a self-service card activation feature, improving customer autonomy and reducing support workload.
Led the design and development of an LLM-based Splunk log-triage workflow intended to streamline how analysts process log data in their daily work.
Owned the product vision and roadmap for a cross-border eCommerce logistics SaaS platform.
Led a cross-functional product team, managing scope, priorities, budget, and delivery timelines.
Translated business and user needs into functional specifications and user stories for development teams.
Maintained and prioritized the product backlog using JIRA, ensuring continuous value delivery.
Worked closely with enterprise clients and partners to align product features with operational and cross-border requirements.
Built Ship24.com from scratch into a scalable cross-border logistics platform within 2 years, serving marketplaces, merchants, and logistics providers.
Delivered a universal shipment tracking API and customs clearance services, supporting international trade operations.
Platform performance in 2023: 16M website visitors; 3000+ active API subscriptions; +30% user growth (YoY); +50% advertising revenue growth (YoY).
Delivered IT projects using Agile / Scrum, supporting delivery execution.
Communicated delivery status and escalated risks and issues to prevent delays.
Worked closely with data engineers, data scientists, and business teams on data-centric and analytics-driven initiatives.
Structured project reporting and communication frameworks to provide visibility to management and executives.
Participated in software and data architecture discussions, with focus on data governance, quality, and traceability.
Supported monthly executive update meetings, contributing to project tracking and prioritization discussions.
Chatbot FINDER: Coordinated development of a chatbot in collaboration with data science teams for the Risk department, enabling faster access to risk-related data.
CRM Data Pipeline Optimization: Supported delivery of a real-time data pipeline built on Big Data infrastructure to optimize Salesforce CRM usage.

AI-Assisted Knowledge Base and PM Tracker: Built an LLM-maintained personal knowledge base using plain Markdown files (inspired by the Karpathy method). Rather than re-discovering knowledge from raw documents on every query (RAG), sources are compiled once into a structured wiki that the LLM keeps updated, cross-referenced, and consistent. Extended into a project-scoped decision engine, maintaining a reliable, coherent, and auditable record of a project's evolution.

Multi-LLM Agent Orchestration Framework: Designed a personal "multi-AI terminal" workflow running Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex in parallel against a shared repository, coordinated via file-based directory contracts and lock-based handoffs. Built a library of specialised sub-agents covering research, critical review, adversarial validation, and project-init / context-sync functions, applying separation of concerns across LLMs to improve output quality and throughput.

Prompt and Agent Library: Maintain a personal Notion-backed library of reusable prompts and agent specifications, covering structured prompting, Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thoughts, adversarial-validation patterns, and persona / permission-to-fail techniques.
Product / Project Management: Agile / Scrum; Roadmap & Backlog Management; IT Governance & Delivery Management; Stakeholder Management; Risk & Dependency Management.

AI, Automation & Productivity: Applied AI for knowledge work and process optimization; prompt engineering (structured prompting, Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thoughts, adversarial validation, persona scaffolding, few-shot examples); multi-step and multi-agent AI workflow design; multi-LLM orchestration (Claude, Gemini, GPT/Codex) with specialized sub-agents; workflow automation with n8n, local LLM experimentation (Ollama); AI enablement (workshop design and facilitation, internal training, prompt and agent libraries, user guides / SOPs); responsible AI usage in regulated environments.
Tools & Platforms: JIRA, Confluence, Notion; API-based systems and third-party / vendor integration; Mobile & Web Platforms; Splunk.
Technical Foundations: SQL; Python; Jenkins; Machine learning / Deep learning fundamentals.

# Tailoring Report - GRADION / IT Project Manager / Senior Project Manager

Date: 2026-07-28
Offer: `job_offers/2026-07-28_gradion_it-project-manager-senior-project-manager/offer.md`
CV: `job_offers/2026-07-28_gradion_it-project-manager-senior-project-manager/tailored_cv/cv_mounier_gradion_it-project-manager-senior-project-manager_v1.md`
Dominant framing: IT Project Manager with technical-consulting overlay

## Role Analysis

The role combines delivery control, client advisory, and commercial awareness. Its strongest hiring signals are end-to-end international software delivery, turning ambiguity into executable scope, early risk escalation with decision-ready recommendations, direct communication across clients and engineering, and practical AI use with human verification. GRADION also expects the Project Manager to understand how Dedicated Team and Fixed-Price economics differ, protect margin and scope, and recognise account-growth opportunities.

## Evidence Map

| Requirement | Importance | Matching evidence from source | Classification | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5+ years in IT project management | Must | 7+ years across BRED, Okoone, and Societe Generale | Verified | Exceeds threshold |
| IT or Computer Science degree | Must | Master's Degree in Computer Science, ESIEA | Verified | Direct match |
| End-to-end IT delivery | Must | BRED end-to-end delivery across core banking, mobile banking, and digital transformation | Verified | Strong match |
| Dedicated Team delivery | Must | Okoone cross-functional product team and BRED international delivery teams | Partially Supported | Team delivery is evidenced, but the named commercial engagement model is not |
| Fixed-Price delivery | Must | Security-audit scope, deliverables, timelines, and pricing at BRED | Partially Supported | Commercial scoping is evidenced, but full Fixed-Price project ownership and margin control are not |
| Translate ambiguous requirements into scope and plans | Must | BRED requirements, scope, priorities, delivery plans, and success criteria, plus Okoone functional specifications | Derived | Wording synthesises documented scope and requirements work |
| Main contact across clients, engineering, and internal stakeholders | Must | BRED primary interface across IT, business stakeholders, vendors, and partners, plus Okoone client-facing advisory work | Verified | Strong match |
| Raise risks early with options and recommendations | Must | Formal risk register, escalation, status reports, and steering-committee decisions at BRED | Derived | Options and recommendations are a measured synthesis of escalation and decision support |
| Change-request and scope-creep control | Must | BRED scope governance and priced security-audit scoping | Partially Supported | No direct source states formal Fixed-Price change-request ownership |
| Budget and margin management | Must | Okoone budget management and BRED commercial security-audit pricing | Partially Supported | Budget evidence exists, margin ownership does not |
| Capacity planning and prioritisation | Must | Cross-functional delivery coordination, MoSCoW prioritisation, roadmap and backlog ownership | Partially Supported | Prioritisation is verified, formal Dedicated Team capacity planning is not |
| International English communication | Must | Fluent English and delivery across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, and US-based teams | Verified | Direct match |
| Cross-cultural teams | Must | International teams and external partners across several regions | Verified | Strong match |
| Daily AI-tool use with judgement | Must | Agentic PM assistant, Splunk triage workflow, human-review criteria, AI workshops, and multi-LLM personal workflow | Verified | Major differentiator |
| Technical or software-development grounding | Preferred | Computer Science Master's, SQL, Python, ML work, API integrations, software-product delivery | Verified | Strong differentiator |
| Business development and account growth | Preferred | Okoone client product presentations and API package sales | Verified | Relevant commercial exposure |
| Travel to client sites | Preferred | Open to international assignments and APAC relocation | Partially Supported | Mobility is verified, past client-site travel is not documented |

## Match Summary

- Strong matches:
  - International end-to-end IT delivery across regulated banking, fintech, SaaS, and digital platforms.
  - Client-facing communication connecting business stakeholders, engineers, QA, cybersecurity, and external vendors.
  - Formal risk governance, steering reporting, release controls, and early escalation.
  - Requirements translation, scope definition, software-development understanding, and API delivery.
  - Practical AI use in live PM workflows with explicit human-review boundaries.
  - Cross-cultural English-speaking team delivery and confirmed relocation interest in Ho Chi Minh City.
- Partial matches:
  - Dedicated Team experience is adjacent but the commercial engagement label is not documented.
  - Fixed-Price experience is adjacent through scope, budget, pricing, and security-audit definition, but project margin ownership is not documented.
  - Capacity planning is adjacent through team coordination and prioritisation, not explicitly confirmed as formal capacity ownership.
- Gaps:
  - Direct evidence of protecting Fixed-Price margin.
  - Direct ownership of formal change requests under a Fixed-Price contract.
  - Past client-site travel is not documented.

## Verification Audit

### Item 1
- Draft claim: "translating business requirements into scope, delivery plans, priorities, and success criteria"
- Classification: Partially Supported
- Why introduced: Mirrors the role's central requirement to convert ambiguity into executable delivery.
- Closest source support: Root CV documents BRED scope management and stakeholder interfacing. Okoone documents translation of business needs into functional specifications and user stories.
- Risk: Low
- Recommended action: Keep

### Item 2
- Draft claim: "presenting options, recommendations, and decision points through recurring status reports and steering committees"
- Classification: Partially Supported
- Why introduced: Aligns risk escalation with GRADION's decision-oriented client style.
- Closest source support: Root CV documents formal risk registers, risk escalation, management reporting, and steering-committee presentations.
- Risk: Low
- Recommended action: Keep

### Item 3
- Draft claim: "open to relocation to Ho Chi Minh City"
- Classification: Partially Supported
- Why introduced: Makes location fit explicit.
- Closest source support: `context/work_eligibility_mobility.md` confirms Ho Chi Minh City as an accepted relocation target. Work-authorisation or sponsorship status for Vietnam is not documented.
- Risk: Low
- Recommended action: Keep

## User-confirmed Additions

- None in this run.

## Keyword Coverage

- Covered: end-to-end IT delivery, client-facing, international delivery, scope, success criteria, risk analysis, options and recommendations, change control, AI tools, software development, stakeholder communication, cross-functional teams, account growth.
- Not covered or used only in the report: Fixed-Price margin ownership, formal Dedicated Team capacity planning, formal Fixed-Price change-request ownership.

## Intentional Omissions

- Fixed-Price project ownership was not claimed because the sources document commercial scoping and budget work, not full contract-margin accountability.
- Dedicated Team engagement ownership was not claimed by name because the sources document long-running cross-functional teams but not the contract model.
- Margin management was omitted because no source confirms responsibility for delivery margin.
- Client-site travel history was omitted because willingness to relocate or travel does not prove past travel.

## Ambiguities

- GRADION advertises both Project Manager and Senior Project Manager in one title. The CV uses Senior IT Project Manager because the candidate's current verified title and experience support it.
- The candidate has strong delivery-model adjacency, but the offer treats named Dedicated Team and Fixed-Price experience as a must-have. The application should not imply this is fully verified unless the candidate can confirm examples.

## Follow-up Questions

1. At Okoone or BRED, did you personally own a Fixed-Price software engagement, including estimates, signed scope, change requests, and delivery margin?
2. Were any of your Okoone or BRED teams operated under a client-funded Dedicated Team contract where you owned capacity, utilisation, and ongoing client alignment?
3. Do you need employer sponsorship or another work-authorisation route for a full-time role in Vietnam?

## Suggested Persistence

- If confirmed, add exact Fixed-Price and Dedicated Team examples, including responsibility boundaries, to `context/skills_addendum.md`.
- Record Vietnam work-authorisation status in `context/work_eligibility_mobility.md`.

## Quality Checklist

- [x] No dates, employers, titles, certifications, tools, or metrics were invented.
- [x] Every non-Verified or non-Derived draft claim appears in the audit.
- [x] No High-risk claim is present in the CV.
- [x] ATS layout is single-column with conventional headings and contact details in the body.
- [x] Bullet caps are respected: BRED 8, Okoone 4, Societe Generale 3.
- [x] Skills use four categorised groups with 12 total items.
- [x] Fixed section order is preserved.
- [x] Prior CV versions were not overwritten.
